claim_a.text: Under the same GPT-3 175B comparison, LoRA uses 10,000 times fewer trainable parameters than full fine-tuning.

claim_b.text: Under the same GPT-3 175B comparison, LoRA uses 10,000 times more trainable parameters than full fine-tuning.

rationale: The conditions and quantity match while the direction is opposite.

claim_a.text: Across the same five LLMs and greedy baseline, Prometheus-2-7B MBR improves AlpacaEval by 3.6 percent on average.

claim_b.text: Across the same five LLMs and greedy baseline, Prometheus-2-7B MBR worsens AlpacaEval by 3.6 percent on average.

rationale: The claims state opposite performance directions under identical conditions.

claim_a.text: Against full GPT-3 175B fine-tuning, LoRA uses 10,000 times fewer trainable parameters and three times less GPU memory.

claim_b.text: Against the same full GPT-3 175B fine-tuning baseline, LoRA uses 10,000 times fewer trainable parameters but five times more GPU memory.

rationale: The parameter conclusion agrees while the GPU-memory conclusion conflicts.

claim_a.text: Relative to greedy decoding across five LLMs, Prometheus MBR improves AlpacaEval by 3.6 percent and MT-Bench by 0.28.

claim_b.text: Relative to the same greedy baseline across the same five LLMs, Prometheus MBR improves AlpacaEval by 3.6 percent but lowers MT-Bench by 0.28.

rationale: The AlpacaEval conclusion agrees and the MT-Bench conclusion is reversed.

claim_a.text: On WikiSQL with LoRA applied to both Wq and Wv at rank one, validation accuracy is 73.4.

claim_b.text: On WikiSQL with LoRA applied only to Wq at rank one, validation accuracy is 68.8.

rationale: The dataset and metric match, but the adapted weight matrices differ.

claim_a.text: Prometheus MBR improves average AlpacaEval performance by 3.6 percent relative to greedy decoding.

claim_b.text: SFR-Embedder MBR reduces average AlpacaEval performance by 1.4 percent relative to greedy decoding.

rationale: The benchmark and baseline match, but the utility metric method differs.

claim_a.text: LoRA does not add inference latency after its low-rank matrices are merged into the pretrained weights.

claim_b.text: Merging the LoRA update into the base weights means LoRA introduces no additional latency during inference.

rationale: Both claims express the same no-extra-latency conclusion.

claim_a.text: In the reported iterative self-training comparison, SFT yields significantly less improvement than DPO.

claim_b.text: For that same iterative self-training experiment, DPO produces larger gains than SFT.

rationale: The statements give the same ordering in inverse wording.

claim_a.text: Adapter layers can increase online inference latency because they are processed sequentially.

claim_b.text: GPT-4o judgments for MT-Bench are generated three times per sample and aggregated by the median.

rationale: The claims concern unrelated mechanisms and evaluations.

claim_a.text: Rank one can be sufficient when LoRA adapts both query and value projection matrices.

claim_b.text: Utility-metric reward hacking may select benchmark-favoured outputs that are worse in actual quality.

rationale: One claim concerns adaptation rank and the other evaluator bias.

claim_a.text: LoRA is an efficient adaptation method for large language models.

claim_b.text: The alternative adaptation approach is more effective.

rationale: The alternative, effectiveness metric and comparison conditions are unspecified.

claim_a.text: MBR decoding produces significant and consistent improvements in the reported instruction-following experiments.

claim_b.text: Its benefits are limited in practice.

rationale: The second claim omits the method referent, metric, dataset and evaluation setting needed for comparison.
